hints: Notice the column headings run from the shortest wavelength $10^{-14}\text{ m}$ on the left to the longest wavelength $10^{2}\text{ m}$ on the right.
Recall the electromagnetic spectrum in order of increasing wavelength: gamma ray, X-ray, ultraviolet, visible, infra-red, microwave, radio wave.

Compare the middle values: check which region $10^{-6}\text{ m}$ and $10^{-2}\text{ m}$ fall in, remembering infra-red is around $10^{-6}\text{ m}$ to $10^{-3}\text{ m}$ and microwave is around $10^{-3}\text{ m}$ to $10^{-1}\text{ m}$.
walkthrough: List the given wavelengths in order: $10^{-14}\text{ m}$, $10^{-10}\text{ m}$, $10^{-6}\text{ m}$, $10^{-2}\text{ m}$, $10^{2}\text{ m}$, so wavelength increases from left to right.
State the governing order for principal radiations by increasing wavelength: gamma rays shortest, then X-rays, then ultraviolet and visible, then infra-red, then microwaves, then radio waves longest.
Match the extremes: $10^{-14}\text{ m}$ is in the gamma-ray region and $10^{2}\text{ m}$ is clearly in the radio-wave region.
Match the middle values: $10^{-10}\text{ m}$ is typical X-ray wavelength, $10^{-6}\text{ m}$ is infra-red, and $10^{-2}\text{ m}$ is microwave.
The only row with gamma ray, X-ray, infra-red, microwave, radio wave in that left-to-right order is row A. This is option A.

A.explanation: Matches the spectrum in order of increasing wavelength: $10^{-14}\text{ m}$ gamma ray, $10^{-10}\text{ m}$ X-ray, $10^{-6}\text{ m}$ infra-red, $10^{-2}\text{ m}$ microwave, $10^{2}\text{ m}$ radio wave.

B.explanation: Reverses the spectrum and misplaces $10^{-2}\text{ m}$, since X-rays have much shorter wavelength near $10^{-10}\text{ m}$, not $10^{-2}\text{ m}$.

C.explanation: Reverses short and long wavelength ends and mislabels $10^{-6}\text{ m}$ and $10^{-2}\text{ m}$, which are infra-red and microwave, not ultraviolet and infra-red.

D.explanation: Mislabels $10^{-14}\text{ m}$ and $10^{-10}\text{ m}$; $10^{-14}\text{ m}$ is shorter than typical X-rays so is gamma ray, and $10^{-10}\text{ m}$ is X-ray, not infra-red.
